complaint.narrative: This collector calls me multiple times a day and has also called my workplace, which I never gave them permission to contact.

allegations: Collector calls multiple times a day
Collector called the customer's workplace without permission

account.account_note: Call log shows 6 calls to customer's personal number in the past 7 days (CONFIRMED — frequent contact, consistent with complaint). No record of any call placed to a workplace or employer number exists in the system; only one phone number (personal, customer-provided) is on file (NOT CONFIRMED — no workplace contact).

transactions.note: 6 calls to personal number in 7-day window. No workplace contact on record.

verification.fact_verification_explanation: The customer reports two problem events. (1) Frequent calls: the call log shows 6 calls to the customer's personal number in a 7-day window, so the frequent contact is confirmed. The log gives the count, not a per-day breakdown, so 'multiple times a day' is supported in substance but not exactly. (2) Call to the workplace: no call to any workplace or employer number appears in the system. Only one number, the customer-provided personal number, is on file, so this is not confirmed. The customer is right about the call frequency. The workplace contact cannot be confirmed from our records. It may have come from another number or channel we do not log, so this is not treated as disproven.
verification.risk_rationale: The claim is partially true, and confirmed call frequency and alleged third-party (workplace) contact are Reg F conduct that rates Medium on its own; no threats, false statements, abusive language, attorney/regulator reference, or hardship/vulnerability are alleged, so the Reg F elevate-to-High bullet does not apply.

policy.text:
# Internal Policy: General Dispute Handling Process

**Applies to:** Any complaint not governed more specifically by another policy in this set (i.e., the default process).

## Standard process
1. **Acknowledge** receipt within 3 business days.
2. **Investigate** — compare the customer's claim against account and transaction records.
3. **Classify** the outcome as one of: confirmed (company error), not confirmed (no error found), partially confirmed (mixed), or unable to verify (insufficient data).
4. **Respond** in writing within 15 calendar days of receipt (consistent with standard regulatory complaint-handling expectations), addressing every distinct allegation raised in the complaint individually — a response that addresses only the primary complaint and ignores a secondary request is incomplete.
5. **Close** the case with a documented root-cause category for internal trend reporting.

## What counts as a complete response
- Every distinct factual allegation is addressed (confirmed, not confirmed, or unable to verify).
- Every distinct request the customer made is addressed (a refund request and an account-closure request in the same complaint both need a response, even if only one is granted).
- The response states a clear next step or outcome — never ends on an open-ended "we are looking into it" with no indication of what happens next, unless the case is genuinely still pending additional information.

## What an analyst or agent may say
- May state what was investigated and the outcome in plain language.
- May NOT close a case as "resolved" if any raised allegation was not actually addressed.

## Escalation trigger
Use the dedicated Escalation Criteria policy (document 09) for attorney/regulator/vulnerability triggers. This document covers only the baseline process for complaints that don't meet those triggers.

*This is an internal, generic policy created for a training/demonstration environment and does not reflect any specific company's actual policy.*

draft.draft_text:
Thank you for reaching out about the calls from the collector. You told us they're calling you multiple times a day and that they called you at your workplace without your permission. That's stressful, especially when it reaches you at work, and we want to give you a clear answer on both points.

The calls to you: We looked at the call history on your account. It shows 6 calls to your personal number within a 7-day window, so we can confirm you've been contacted frequently. The history gives us the total number of calls, not how many came on each day, so we can't tell you from it how many fell on any single day.

The call to your workplace: We don't see any call to a workplace or employer number in our records. The only number we have on file for you is your personal number, so we haven't been able to confirm this part of your complaint. If you can tell us which number was called, the date and time, and anything else you remember about the call, please send it to us and we'll review it.

Where things stand: We've confirmed the frequency of calls to your personal number. We haven't been able to confirm the workplace call from the records we have. Please feel free to send us more information at any time, and we'll review it. You can reply to this message or call us at the number on your account.

Case reference: SYN-P03.

verifier.completeness_check: pass — both allegations are addressed individually: (1) frequent calls, in 'The calls to you' paragraph, and (2) the workplace call, in 'The call to your workplace' paragraph. None are missing.
verifier.groundedness_check: pass — The '6 calls to your personal number within a 7-day window' figure, the absence of any workplace or employer number in the records, and the personal number being the only one on file all match the verification output. The draft also follows the verification's caveat that the call log gives a total, not a per-day breakdown, and it does not claim the workplace call is disproven. No invented facts, dates, or amounts, and no claim that any remedy has been granted or processed.
verifier.policy_authorization_check: pass — The draft states no remedy (remedy_stated and referral_stated are null) and promises nothing beyond reviewing any additional information the customer sends. Nothing exceeds the authority in the cited policy.
verifier.prohibited_language_check: pass — No fault admission beyond confirmed fact (it confirms only the call frequency, which the verification supports). No guarantees about the future, no legal conclusions, no unauthorized promises, and nothing that discourages the customer from other channels. The empathy line ('That's stressful...') is measured, not performative or an admission of fault.
verifier.tone_structure_check: pass — The draft follows Policy 11 order: a specific opening acknowledgment, findings for each allegation, a clear outcome (call frequency confirmed, workplace call not confirmed), next steps (send the number, date, and time, and reply or call), and the case reference SYN-P03. It uses second person and plain language, has short paragraphs, and treats each allegation separately, as required for a multi-allegation complaint.
